sections.title: Four Clashes, One Dream: The Morning's Matchups

items.headline: Spain's Masterclass Begins Against Cabo Verde's Historic Moment
items.body: <cite index="4-2">Spain are playing in their 13th successive World Cup</cite>, while <cite index="4-6">Cabo Verde secured qualification at their seventh attempt</cite>. <cite index="3-10,3-11">Cabo Verde's attack relies on direct counters and wing pace, with 35-year-old captain Ryan Mendes providing leadership and attacking quality</cite>. Spain will dominate possession against an organized underdog seeking a historic upset.
items.h2h_context: First World Cup meeting. Spain heavily favored as world-class team.
items.watch_key: Spain's control vs. Cabo Verde's counter-press; Mendes as escape valve in midfield.

items.headline: Belgium's Salah Duel: Garcia's Red Devils Face Egypt's Qualifier Elite
items.body: <cite index="8-5">Belgium will look to improve on their third-place finish in 2018 under Rudi Garcia</cite>. <cite index="8-9">Egypt's star forward Salah netted nine goals in their qualifying campaign</cite>. <cite index="12-2">Belgium defeated Egypt 2-1 in a 2022 friendly and won 3-0 in a 2018 friendly</cite>—but Egypt arrives as CAF Group A winner.
items.h2h_context: Belgium leads recent H2H (2 wins, 0 losses). Egypt seeking to prove qualifier form.
items.watch_key: Salah vs. Belgium's defense; midfield intensity; set-piece threats from both sides.

items.headline: Uruguay's Bielsa Against Saudi Arabia's Upset Legacy
items.body: <cite index="4-1">Uruguay secured their passage with a comfortable fourth-place finish in CONMEBOL qualifying under Marcelo Bielsa</cite>. <cite index="23-1">Uruguay beat Saudi Arabia 1-0 in the 2018 World Cup and drew 1-1 in a 2014 friendly</cite>. But <cite index="16-17">Saudi Arabia return with memories of their famous 2022 win over Argentina</cite>—expect a disciplined, counter-attacking display.
items.h2h_context: Uruguay unbeaten vs. Saudi Arabia (1W, 1D). Saudi Arabia hungry for another upset.
items.watch_key: Bielsa's pressing intensity; Saudi Arabia's defensive discipline; set pieces near the box.

items.headline: Iran's Taremi vs. New Zealand's Oceanic Challenge
items.body: <cite index="8-12">Iran star striker Mehdi Taremi scored a brace in a draw against Uzbekistan that sealed qualification</cite>. <cite index="10-6">The two sides have never met before</cite>. <cite index="8-14,8-15">New Zealand secured their berth as the first OFC team to receive a direct qualification spot</cite>, but face a vastly more experienced AFC opponent.
items.h2h_context: First World Cup meeting. Iran heavy favorites based on FIFA ranking and qualification form.
items.watch_key: Taremi's finishing; New Zealand's defensive shape; Iran's transition tempo.

items.headline: Spain and Uruguay Set Knockout Race—Cape Verde's Third-Place Hopes Real
items.body: <cite index="16-19,16-20,16-21">Uruguay look set to provide Spain's main challenge for top spot, with Spain expected to finish top two as tournament favorites</cite>. <cite index="20-3,20-6">With 48 teams, the top two in each group advance plus eight best third-place teams—giving Cape Verde a genuine knockout path if they stay competitive</cite>. Saudi Arabia can upset either heavyweight but Saudi Arabia likely finish third or lower.
items.implications: Spain-Uruguay clash on June 26 becomes potential de facto Group H final.

items.headline: Belgium Favored, But Egypt's Qualifying Form Could Flip the Table
items.body: <cite index="8-8">Egypt finished top of Group A in CAF qualifying, winning eight matches</cite>. Belgium's experience and tactical flexibility give them advantage, but Egypt arrives as African champions of their qualifying group. <cite index="10-3">Top two teams advance along with eight best third-placed sides</cite>—Iran-New Zealand loser likely finishes third; winner could threaten Belgium or Egypt.
items.implications: Belgium-Egypt winner likely secures top spot; loser still has qualification pathway via third place.

items.headline: Early Wins Lock Down Spots; Draws Create Drama for Matchday 3
items.body: <cite index="21-3,21-5,21-6">Top two advance to Round of 32, with knockout matchups pitting Group H winner vs. Group J runner-up and Group H runner-up vs. Group J winner</cite>. Teams winning on Day 1 gain psychological advantage and goal-difference buffer. Close results in both groups mean June 21 becomes crunch time for qualification odds.
items.implications: Results today reshape entire second matchday narrative; first-game momentum is critical.

sections.title: What to Watch: Tactical Angles and Drama Triggers

items.headline: Can Spain Control Cabo Verde Without Overcommitting?
items.body: Spain's possession dominance meets Cabo Verde's compact, disciplined defensive block. <cite index="3-10,3-13">Cape Verde relies on direct counters and opportunistic pace from players like Jovane Cabral and Willy Semedo</cite>. Watch for Spain's width exploitation and whether they can avoid being caught on fast breaks. A 2-0 or 3-0 win sets tone; a 1-0 scrappy result signals vulnerability.
items.critical_moments: Cabo Verde's first 15 minutes pressing; Spain's set-piece conversion; counter-attack transitions.

items.headline: Egypt's Qualifying Dominance vs. Belgium's Experience: Who Dictates Play?
items.body: <cite index="8-5">Rudi Garcia's Belgium side hopes to improve on 2018 third place</cite>, while Egypt arrives fresh off dominant CAF qualifying. Belgium's depth and UEFA pedigree typically trump African qualifiers, but Salah can punish sloppiness. Watch tactical formation battles—does Egypt press high or sit compact? Does Belgium dominate midfield tempo?
items.critical_moments: Salah's pressing intensity; Belgium's wide play vs. Egyptian wing defense; early card accumulation.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia's Discipline vs. Uruguay's Intensity: Bielsa's Pressure Test
items.body: <cite index="4-1">Uruguay embraced 'Bielsa-ball' to secure their passage</cite>. Saudi Arabia's 2022 Argentina upset was built on compact defense and clinical counters. Today tests whether Bielsa's high press overwhelms Saudi discipline or Saudi Arabia's resilience frustrates Uruguay. Early goal swings momentum dramatically—a Saudi equalizer forces Uruguay to adapt mid-match.
items.critical_moments: First 20 minutes pressing tempo; Saudi Arabia's first counter attempt; card count at halftime.

items.headline: Iran's Offensive Swagger vs. New Zealand's Defensive Compactness
items.body: <cite index="8-12">Mehdi Taremi's brace against Uzbekistan sealed Iran's qualification</cite>, signaling confidence in attack. New Zealand, as OFC minnow, will defend and seek set pieces. Iran's dominance expected, but New Zealand's grit could keep it closer than expected. Watch Taremi's positioning and whether Iran's midfield controls possession or New Zealand's shape prevents dangerous space.
items.critical_moments: Taremi's shooting opportunities; New Zealand's defensive shape holds/breaks; substitute impact late.
